content.intro: Learn saving forms to the database through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Saving Forms to the Database matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines saving forms to the database as part of forms and user input. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: form.save(); commit=False; Assigning fields not supplied by the user; Saving many-to-many relationships; Ensuring ownership and permissions server-side. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: form.save()
items.text: form.save() shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: commit=False
items.text: For commit=False, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Assigning fields not supplied by the user
items.text: Assigning fields not supplied by the user affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Saving many-to-many relationships
items.text: Saving many-to-many relationships affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Ensuring ownership and permissions server-side
items.text: Model permissions are a useful starting point but do not automatically enforce ownership of every individual record. Scope each lookup and mutation to the caller’s authorized objects.

Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
